---
title: Script
description: "A program that connects, does its job and exits: uploading data, exporting results, a batch analysis. connect(Mikro), several clients at once, sync and async, and typed GraphQL for operations the client does not wrap."
type: guide
---

The simplest way to use the platform: a Python file that connects, does one job and exits.
Uploading a folder of images, exporting a table of results, re-running an analysis over last
week's datasets.

## Use it when

- The program has a **beginning and an end**.
- You run it yourself, or a scheduler does (see [Unattended](/docs/build/connect/unattended)).
- Nothing else needs to call it.

## The shape

```python
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr

from arkitekt import connect
from mikro import Mikro, dataset_arrays

volume = xr.DataArray(np.random.rand(1, 20, 256, 256).astype("float32"), dims=("c", "z", "y", "x"))

with connect(Mikro, identifier="volume-upload") as mikro:
    folder = mikro.create_folder(name="examples")
    level_zero, scales = dataset_arrays(volume, levels=3, method="mean")
    dataset = mikro.create_array_dataset(
        data=level_zero, scales=scales, name="random volume",
        axes=["c", "z", "y", "x"], folder=folder.id,
    )
    print(dataset.id)
```

- **The identifier** is the app you approve, once, and what the platform records as having created
  the data. It defaults to the file's name. Give it one that says what the script is for.
- **Nothing connects before the block.** Entering logs in and connects, leaving disconnects.
- **Several clients** come back as a tuple, in order: `with connect(Mikro, Fluss) as (mikro, fluss):`.
- **Async** is the same object: `async with connect(Mikro) as mikro:`, and every client method has
  an `a`-prefixed twin (`await mikro.acreate_folder(...)`).

## When the client has no method for it

Every client wraps the operations most people need. For anything else, write the GraphQL query
yourself and generate a typed function for it:

```bash
uv run arkitekt gen init --client mikro     # a GraphQL config and a folder for your queries
uvx --with mikro turms gen                  # generate code from them
```

The generated functions use the connected client, so call them inside the `connect(...)` block.
See [GraphQL](/docs/build/python/graphql).

## What to watch

- **Returned objects are snapshots.** Setting an attribute changes nothing on the server. Call the
  matching mutation.
- **Large data goes in as datasets**, with a pyramid if anyone will look at it, and with the axes
  named. [Uploading data from a script](/docs/build/python/examples/uploads) shows the axis-order
  mistakes to avoid.
- **A script is not resumed.** If it dies halfway, what it already created stays and the rest is
  not done. For long multi-step jobs that start tasks on other apps, see
  [Workflow](/docs/build/apps/workflow).
